title: Our Efforts Towards the Summit of Victory!
translatorNote: This translation is intended to carry Kalaignar's voice into clear, contemporary English rather than recast the letter as literary or academic prose. It preserves the source's argument, political directness, rhetorical questions, repetition, irony, factual detail, and paragraph order. Names, dates, figures, quotations, and intentional English expressions are retained. Where Tamil idiom cannot be reproduced literally without sounding unnatural, the English follows its sense and rhetorical force without adding claims absent from the source. The original Tamil is reproduced in full below the translation and remains the authoritative text. `Udanpirappē` is retained in Tamil transliteration rather than flattened into “brother,” “sister,” or “comrade.” Literally evoking “one born alongside me,” Kalaignar uses it as a distinctive address of shared identity, equality, affection, and solidarity within the movement. Letter-specific notes: 1. **TESO** is the Tamil Eelam Supporters Organisation. 2. **Thirteenth Amendment** refers to the amendment to Sri Lanka’s Constitution associated with the 1987 Indo–Sri Lanka Accord; the translation follows the letter’s own framing and chronology. 3. The source prints the quoted English sentence from Clause 2.14 of the Accord; it is preserved exactly. 4. Scan comparison corrected five canonical artefacts: `உறுதிஅளித்துக்` → `உறுதியளித்துக்` and `உரிமைஅளிப்பது` → `உரிமை அளிப்பது` on PDF 156; and `“டெசோ” .`, `ஆர்ப் பாட்டம்`, and `அதற் கான` on PDF 161.
paragraphs: Today, 26 July 2013, newspapers such as Dina Thanthi, Dinamani and Janasakthi have reported, citing a Government press release, that the Prime Minister has written to the Chief Minister of Tamil Nadu assuring her that there has been no change in the Union Government’s position on the Sri Lankan question and that its work will continue until autonomy is secured for the Tamils.
To explain in detail, in the letter he wrote to the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister on 16 July 2013, the Prime Minister stated:

“Thank you for your letter dated 14 July 2013 concerning possible changes proposed in Sri Lanka in relation to the Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution. There has been no change in the Union Government’s position on the devolution of political powers and the granting of autonomy in Sri Lanka. It has long been our demand that an appropriate environment be created in which all communities in Sri Lanka—particularly the Sri Lankan Tamils—may live together and be entrusted with a leading role. Our work will continue until such autonomy is granted to the Sri Lankan Tamils.”
The contents of the Prime Minister’s letter offer us some comfort.

As soon as it came to our attention that the Sri Lankan Government was attempting to dilute the very basis of the Thirteenth Amendment and reduce it to something lifeless, I wrote a detailed letter to the Prime Minister on 9 June 2013. In it I said:

“You are aware that the Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution of Sri Lanka was the direct outcome of an agreement between India and Sri Lanka. Against the background of the bitter experience that none of the earlier agreements entered into by Sri Lankan Tamils with the Sinhalese were implemented, we in India assured the Sri Lankan Tamils that the Rajiv–Jayewardene Accord would be implemented. President Mahinda Rajapaksa’s brother and Sri Lankan Defence Secretary Gotabaya Rajapaksa has already called for the repeal of the Thirteenth Amendment. It is now the duty and responsibility of the Government of India to intervene directly and ensure the full implementation of the Rajiv–Jayewardene Accord. This will ease the path towards a settlement of the conflict and ethnic reconciliation. At this critical moment, India must not remain a silent spectator to developments in Sri Lanka. I seek your intervention to protect the rights and lives of the Tamils there.”
Prime Minister Dr Manmohan Singh replied immediately on 11 June 2013:

“I have received your letter of 9 June concerning the Thirteenth Amendment to the Constitution of Sri Lanka. Although this is a decision to be taken jointly by the various political parties in Sri Lanka, we will certainly consider its implications and convey our views to the Sri Lankan Government. You are aware that the Government of India has been working on the principle that all sections in Sri Lanka, including the Sri Lankan Tamils, should obtain their due rights and live in harmony.”

Thus, the same issue on which I wrote in detail to the Prime Minister on 9 June and received his explanatory reply on the eleventh was raised by our Chief Minister in a letter dated 14 July. The Prime Minister replied to her on 16 July, and it is that letter which has appeared in the Tamil Nadu newspapers today, 26 July.

It was not only my letter. When representatives of the Tamil National Alliance met the Prime Minister in Delhi on 18 June 2013 and asked him to prevent measures that would dilute the Thirteenth Amendment, newspapers reported at the time that he told them: “We will not abandon the Sri Lankan Tamils; steps will be taken to protect them.”

Nor did the Prime Minister write only to me. In response to a letter sent on 21 June 2013 by Comrade Sitaram Yechury, the Communist Party of India (Marxist) leader in the Rajya Sabha, on the Sri Lankan Tamil question, the Prime Minister replied on 10 July that he was aware of Yechury’s concerns about attempts to dilute the Thirteenth Amendment and that efforts were being made to ensure that Tamils and members of other communities in Sri Lanka were treated equally and with self-respect.
The letters written by the Prime Minister on the Sri Lankan Tamil question—to me, to Comrade Yechury, and now to the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister—give us hope.

In 1987, India and Sri Lanka entered into an agreement for the devolution of powers to Sri Lanka’s Provinces. The Sri Lankan Government is now attempting to amend its Constitution in a manner that violates that agreement. The DMK therefore insists that the Union Government intervene at once and exert strong pressure for the implementation of the Rajiv–Jayewardene Accord as the first step in preparing the path towards a complete and permanent political settlement of the Sri Lankan Tamil question.
Following my letter to the Prime Minister, the first resolution adopted at the meeting of TESO held at Anna Arivalayam on 16 July 2013 stated:

India’s National Security Adviser Shivshankar Menon recently visited Sri Lanka and met President Rajapaksa. In the statement subsequently issued by the Indian High Commission in Sri Lanka, it was said: “India wishes to ensure that all citizens of Sri Lanka, including the Tamils, live with equality, equal justice and self-respect. For an early political settlement of the ethnic question, Sri Lanka must honour the promise it gave India and the international community and provide devolution of powers going beyond the Thirteenth Amendment. Shivshankar Menon emphasised this to President Rajapaksa on India’s behalf. We hope that the election in the Northern Province will be held freely, fairly and credibly. The question of attacks on Indian fishermen was also discussed with President Rajapaksa. It was agreed that, under all circumstances, action must be guided by humanity and without resort to violence.”

The Tamils have lived for ages in the Northern and Eastern parts of Sri Lanka and are among the island’s original inhabitants. Yet their fundamental rights have been denied and they are treated as second-class citizens. Their many successive forms of struggle have not produced results; the Sri Lankan Government’s repression has forced lakhs to live like slaves in their own land and many more lakhs to seek refuge in India and other countries.
Clause 2.14 of the Rajiv–Jayewardene Accord states:
“The Government of India will underwrite and guarantee the resolutions and co-operate in the implementation of these proposals.”
That is, the Government of India signed the agreement with Sri Lanka accepting responsibility for, guaranteeing and cooperating in its implementation.

No country has the authority unilaterally to violate or alter an agreement concluded between two nations, particularly when India’s interests are also embodied in it. We have already pointed out that Basil Rajapaksa’s announcement is contrary to internationally accepted practice.
It is at this moment that the Prime Minister’s letter on this issue has reached the Tamil Nadu Chief Minister.

There was a time when Jayalalithaa moved a resolution in the Tamil Nadu Legislative Assembly—on 16 April 2002—demanding that LTTE leader Prabhakaran be arrested and brought to India. She has now forgotten all that and written an urgent letter to the Prime Minister asking that the Thirteenth Amendment not be diluted. The Prime Minister has replied, and newspapers have reported it. From this, everyone may understand the importance the Sri Lankan Tamil question has acquired.

When the same Jayalalithaa moved a resolution in the Assembly calling for economic sanctions against Sri Lanka, some people leapt between heaven and earth as though Tamil Eelam itself had already been won. Yet now, when she has written to the Prime Minister about the Thirteenth Amendment, they have not opened their mouths. We cannot forget that they once rushed forward claiming that they alone represented the Sri Lankan Tamil cause, while today one must search to discover where they are.

The Thirteenth Amendment is not a complete political solution to the Eelam Tamil question. TESO’s position is that the solution best suited to the welfare of Eelam Tamils is to conduct a referendum among Eelam Tamils living in Sri Lanka and in all other countries and determine the outcome according to their views.
Even so, TESO considers that the Rajiv–Jayewardene Accord should at least serve as an interim measure.

Having set out all these important positions, TESO also adopted resolutions insisting that India should not participate in the forthcoming Commonwealth Conference in Sri Lanka; that Tamil Nadu fishermen must be protected; and that Sinhala settlement in Tamil regions of Sri Lanka must be stopped.

To press these resolutions, TESO has decided to conduct mass Tamil demonstrations in every district headquarters across Tamil Nadu on 8 August. I shall lead the demonstration in Chennai along with Professor Suba Veerapandian; Tamilar Thalaivar Veeramani will lead in Madurai; DMK Treasurer Thalapathi M. K. Stalin in Tiruchirappalli; Thol. Thirumavalavan in Tiruvallur; and other DMK frontline leaders in the remaining districts. The announcements have already been issued.
Udanpirappē, I know that you are working with vigilance and dedication to fulfil your duty and make the 8 August demonstration a success, as always!
With affection, M.K. 27 July 2013
